listing.name: Super Mario 64 / SM64 Co-op DX
listing.summary: Use an upstream-prepared Super Mario 64 / SM64 Co-op DX player with matching originals; runtime maintenance and player data stay upstream-owned.

steps.title: Keep the matching original
steps.instruction: Use your own unchanged US Super Mario 64 game in big-endian .z64 format. Drag the .z64 file into the game window or place a copy beside the game program before opening it. Keep your original separately. The game can copy it to your profile as baserom.us.z64. If a copy already exists there, the game keeps it when you select another file.

steps.title: Prepare the Windows game
steps.instruction: Unpack the complete Windows ZIP into a writable folder and finish the original-file setup. Keep the game program, lang, dynos, mods and libraries together. Add the working sm64coopdx.exe to Portcove with its containing folder as the start folder and retain your existing launch options.

steps.title: Play or replace your working game
steps.instruction: After adding your Windows or Linux game, choose Play. Use upstream tools to replace the game or manage its saves. Removing the Portcove registration leaves the game and data in place. Close the game and its updater before replacing files.

steps.title: Open the Linux or Steam Deck game
steps.instruction: Unpack the complete x64 Linux ZIP and run sm64coopdx from that folder so it can find its bundled libraries. If Portcove offers Use an existing installation, select the working Linux sm64coopdx program and set the unpacked folder as its start folder. The game needs glibc 2.34, GLIBCXX 3.4.29, OpenGL, SDL2, zlib and curl. The separate SteamOS archive in v1.5.1 has the same requirements and different default settings. The publisher directs Steam Deck players to the Linux package from v1.6 onward.

steps.title: Open the macOS app
steps.instruction: Choose the Intel or Apple Silicon ZIP that matches your Mac and keep the complete sm64coopdx.app. Start it directly and drag your original .z64 file into the game window. The v1.5.1 game requires macOS 11 or later. Its bundled updater requires macOS 12 or later.

warnings: To move to v1.5.1 on Linux or Mac, replace the game using the complete upstream archive after backing up your actual profile. Upstream requires a manual update to replace the earlier updater.

references.title: Keep the game version and data you use
references.instruction: Before explicit Play, preserve the actual existing user profile and creating runtime. On Windows the upstream default checks %APPDATA%/sm64coopdx and can instead reuse a populated %APPDATA%/sm64ex-coop folder; an existing --savepath override changes that selection. Preserve both relevant roots and the actual selected path, copied ROM, saves, configuration, mods and caches. A new executable folder does not isolate these profiles. Do not change the path, adopt populated legacy data, add mods or migrate profiles through this guide. Upstream can start its own updater and successor process; close all game/updater windows and confirm they stopped before copying or replacing files.

references.title: Find your Linux or Mac profile
references.instruction: The game uses SDL’s per-user data folder. On Linux look in $XDG_DATA_HOME or ~/.local/share. On Mac look in ~/Library/Application Support. The game can reuse a populated sm64ex-coop folder when sm64coopdx is empty. Preserve the actual folder with your original copy, saves, mods and settings. If you use --savepath, preserve that selected folder.

references.title: Check the original game file
references.instruction: The v1.5.1 game accepts the big-endian US original with MD5 20b854b239203baf6c961b850a4a51a2. Other regions, byte-swapped images and modified files are different inputs.

presentation.manual_preparation: Use the complete official v1.5.1 Windows package and finish normal upstream ROM setup in your own writable player folder. Keep lang, dynos, mods, libraries and all companions together. Register the already working sm64coopdx.exe with its containing folder as working directory, preserving any already reviewed literal arguments. coopdx_updater.exe is the upstream updater, not the selected game player. Use the selected player’s containing folder as working directory and keep the already working literal arguments; do not invent shell commands. You and upstream own this external runtime and all original/game/player data. Registration binds your explicitly selected executable, working directory and literal arguments; it does not authenticate a curated immutable package or original. Play requires your explicit intent. Removing the Portcove registration preserves every external file. Managed Update, Backup, Rollback, migration and external deletion are unavailable. Finish upstream setup yourself and register only the existing working player; no successful setup, gameplay or state compatibility is claimed by this guide.
